Reason: The chest X-ray demonstrates a larger left-sided pleural effusion compared to the right, along with an aortic valve prosthesis that appears atypically positioned or tilted. This malposition is clinically associated with paravalvular leak and subsequent heart failure, which explains the acute respiratory symptoms and pulmonary edema/effusions better than consolidation alone.
